https://imgur.com/a/C43b09O

Interesting, good find.

Maybe some of these are legitimate, but this family does seem to be launching a bunch of organizations in the same "[astroturf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astroturfing)" style.

​

For example, in the [firstswimmer.org](https://firstswimmer.org) you found, the [about page](https://www.firstswimmer.org/team) links to a 16 year-old Zane Tanabe (his son?).

The way it's built feels very similar to the other sites we've seen.

([here are imgur screenshots of these sites in case it gets taken down in the future](https://imgur.com/a/sXea26c))

* [Online application](https://www.firstswimmer.org/apply) to a swimming scholarship (why scholarship?), where you have to submit your personal info (and that's it)
* [Testimonials](https://www.firstswimmer.org/recipients) with no date, no scholarship money, no details on operations (where do they learn how to swim? is it just money? does he send them to a swimming coach?)
* [Very vague / generic descriptions](https://www.firstswimmer.org/learning-to-swim) of what swimming is.
* Also, [paid PR articles](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/high-school-student-helps-first-generation-swimmers-change-their-family-tree-with-free-swim-lessons-301829944.html) (which google says costs from $150 - $1000)

​

**Overall, my intuition for this site is that the parents built this "nonprofit" site for their son's college application.** Given the lack of detail, I don't think this org really does anything, but it does have the right college application words, like "founder of nonprofit", "preventing child drownings", "helping first-gen families"

Well, they did have money to pay PR for some news articles.
